input: Which 4 biomarkers affect patient 56's naive bayes prediction most strongly at 1:3? For each, use the model's overall pattern to say whether a higher or lower value would be associated with less push toward depression.
output:
<PLAN>
BINDINGS = {"patient":56,"model":"naive bayes","ratio":"1:3","k":4}
P1 = RETRIEVE(relation="local_shap", patient=$patient, model=$model, ratio=$ratio, feature=ALL, fields=["value","direction"])
P2 = RANK(input=P1, key="absolute_local_shap", order="descending", top_k=$k)
P3 = RETRIEVE(relation="global_shap_tendency", model=$model, ratio=$ratio, features=P2.features)
P4 = APPLY_RULE(inputs=[P2,P3], rule="if increasing feature lowers SHAP -> increase; if increasing feature raises SHAP -> decrease")
</PLAN>
<DECOMPOSITION>
Step 1: Retrieve the patient-specific local SHAP values and select the 4 largest absolute effects.
Sub-question: For patient 56 in naive bayes trained at 1:3, which 4 biomarkers have the largest absolute local SHAP values?  # Type: searching
Step 2: Retrieve the global SHAP tendency for each selected biomarker.
Sub-question: For those 4 selected biomarkers in naive bayes trained at 1:3, as each biomarker value increases, does its global SHAP tendency increase or decrease the depression prediction?  # Type: searching
Step 3: Apply the SHAP-to-direction mapping to each selected biomarker.
Sub-question: For each selected biomarker, map a decreasing global SHAP tendency to INCREASE and an increasing global SHAP tendency to DECREASE, reporting model-based directions only.  # Type: aggregation
</DECOMPOSITION>
